name: onelake-studio
description: Browse and query Microsoft Fabric OneLake Iceberg tables with DuckDB, and open Power BI semantic models, signed in with your VS Code Microsoft account.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: OneLake Studio never reads or executes workspace files; everything it touches lives in OneLake and its own storage.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Browse and query OneLake Iceberg tables with DuckDB, signed in with the Microsoft account VS Code already holds — you register nothing.
[Sign in to OneLake](command:onelakeStudio.signIn)

onelakeStudio.tenantId.patternErrorMessage: A directory (tenant) ID is a GUID, e.g. 72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47.
onelakeStudio.tenantId.markdownDescription: Directory (tenant) GUID to sign in against. Leave empty for your home tenant; set it to reach a tenant you are a guest in. Machine-scoped on purpose: a setting that steers *authentication* must not be overridable by a workspace's own `.vscode/settings.json`.

onelakeStudio.catalogTtlMinutes.markdownDescription: How old a listing (workspaces, items, tables, Files/) may be before it is refreshed. The last-known answer is ALWAYS served instantly from disk; once it is older than this, a background refresh fetches the current one and the tree redraws if it changed. `0` refreshes behind every read. **Refresh** in the tree re-reads in the foreground. A table's own metadata has its own window, `tableMetadataTtlHours`. Applies after the window is reloaded.

onelakeStudio.tableMetadataTtlHours.markdownDescription: How old a table's Iceberg metadata (its snapshot, schema and stats, from the catalog's slowest call) may be before it is refreshed, in hours. A table you have opened before opens from disk without asking the catalog; past this age it is refreshed behind you and a new snapshot shows one open later. **Refresh** on its lakehouse (or the whole tree) re-reads it at once. Applies after the window is reloaded.

onelakeStudio.prefetchMetadata.markdownDescription: When a lakehouse's **Tables** node is opened, read each table's Iceberg metadata in the background (two at a time, skipping what is already cached), so the first click on a table is a disk read rather than a wait on the Iceberg catalog — which can take seconds per table. Turn off to read a table's metadata only when it is clicked.

onelakeStudio.engineMemoryLimit.patternErrorMessage: A DuckDB memory size, e.g. 4GB or 512MB.
onelakeStudio.engineMemoryLimit.markdownDescription: Most memory DuckDB may use, e.g. `4GB`. Empty means a quarter of this machine's RAM — DuckDB's own default is 80%, which is too much for the extension host every other extension shares. Bigger queries spill to a temp directory instead of failing. Applies the next time the engine starts.

onelakeStudio.diskCacheMaxGB.markdownDescription: How much of what DuckDB reads from OneLake (table data, manifests, metadata) is kept on disk, in GB, so a table read once is read from this machine afterwards — even after a restart, with no request to OneLake. Tables only: an Iceberg table's files never change once written, while `Files/` objects can, so those are always read live. Kept per Microsoft account; the oldest is dropped past this size when the engine starts. **Clear Cached OneLake Data** empties it. Applies the next time the engine starts.

onelakeStudio.semanticModelsFolder.markdownDescription: Where a semantic model's `.bim` is downloaded the first time you click it in the tree: `<folder>/<workspace>/<model>.bim`. After that it opens from this file (the tree marks it *cached*); **Download Again** fetches it fresh. Empty means `OneLakeStudio/semantic-models` in your home directory. The extension writes nothing to Fabric or OneLake.
